request: Add offline substring search to this Python catalog using the application's src/database.py connection. Search must be accent insensitive and Unicode casefold insensitive, without changing displayed titles: cafe finds Café Racer, STRASSE finds Die Straße, and interior query afe finds Café Racer. Query xyz finds no records. An empty query returns no matches. Search order is stable by ID and duplicate titles preserve distinct IDs. The fixed initial catalog fits in memory (at most 5000 titles), search needs no external service, no fuzzy ranking and no new dependency. A previous design note suggests SQLite FTS5 trigram or LIKE if they meet these semantics on this binding; that is a proposal, not an accepted requirement. Verify the chosen mechanism at its real boundary when needed, and retain implementation and consumer checks as future work. Temporary local experiments on disposable data are authorized. Existing tests must remain passing.

# Supplied discovery

This is a constructed planning fixture. Source, tests and data are present; the baseline suite passed. Only existing behavior was tested. No new feature, atomicity or search acceptance is implied. No earlier decision experiment is supplied.

# Architecture

## Stack

Python standard library: sqlite3 and unicodedata. No service, dependency addition or fuzzy ranking.

## Structure

src/database.py owns connection creation. data/catalog.json supplies [(1,"Café Racer"),(2,"Die Straße"),(3,"Café Racer")]. Planned src/search.py exposes search_catalog(connection,query) -> list of (id,original_title) tuples. Planned tests/test_search.py owns regression and public API consumer cases. No CLI or screen is specified.

Namespace map (AD-5): local Python only; src is an existing package, database.connect is existing public adapter. Planned src.search.search_catalog is the single new public name, _search_key is module-private; it imports unicodedata and uses only the supplied connection. tests.test_search.SearchTests imports it inside test setup/test methods so collection loads before missing implementation and fails RED explicitly. No export from src/__init__.py, runtime monkeypatch, external name or empty package is required. Fixture helpers stay private to tests/test_search.py; consumer example lives in README.md.

Data map (AD-6): authoritative read-only seed data/catalog.json, integer unique IDs and verbatim text titles. Ephemeral schema v1 catalog(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,title TEXT NOT NULL), nonunique titles, no relationships or extra index. Caller/fixture owns CREATE and parameterized INSERT on a disposable connection; search owns reads only. No existing production schema/persistent target is supplied: no durable schema version marker, backfill or migration is introduced for this ephemeral setup. Retain source JSON; close connections to discard test data; no sensitive data, backup or remote quota. Capacity assumption <=5000 titles is supplied by request. If durable storage is introduced, revisit versioning/retention/migration before dependent work.

## Conventions

Observed exemplars: src/database.py small explicit function/std-library import; tests/test_baseline.py unittest.TestCase/assertEqual. Match these. No existing schema/loader/search pattern; new contracts below are explicit design choices.

## Interfaces and boundaries

Caller supplies an initialized application SQLite connection. Proposed minimal table contract: catalog(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,title TEXT NOT NULL), seeded verbatim from data/catalog.json. No schema/loader exists yet; plan assigns the smallest fixture/consumer initializer before dependent checks. No production migration is required.
Read SELECT id,title FROM catalog ORDER BY id through that connection. Compute separate comparison keys and filter by literal substring; return original tuples. No hidden connection, rewriting titles, deduplication, ranking or SQL-error-to-empty conversion.
Normalization policy: NFD, casefold, NFD again, remove Unicode mark categories M*. Apply identically to titles and query. Empty normalized query -> []; whitespace stays literal. Canonical accent removal is not universal transliteration. Each call reads the fixed <=5000-title catalog, computes temporary keys, then discards them: no persistent search cache or invalidation requirement. Errors propagate; connection lifecycle belongs to caller.

## Real-boundary checks

RB-1, decision feasibility OBSERVED: disposable SQLite through src.database.connect, reverse-inserted supplied fixture. Normalized Python substring gives cafe/afe -> [1,3], STRASSE -> [2], xyz/empty -> [], exact unchanged titles/IDs; 5000 matching rows ordered. Raw SQLite LIKE returned [] for cafe and STRASSE. FTS5 is untested and not selected. Exact source and outputs in run scratch/search-decision.py and scratch/search-decision-output.json. This is not implemented feature evidence.

RB-2, PLANNED, implement/test owner: retained actual-binding cases in environment.md. Fresh connection/schema/seed per test; compare public API full tuples to literal expected values, use second connection [(9,"Other")] against hidden fixture reads, compare rows/schema/change counters before and after. Target local, no retained state. Tests must fail on base/missing function, raw LIKE and lower-only replacements.

RB-3, PLANNED, test/handoff owner: consumer imports src.search.search_catalog, opens src.database.connect(), creates stated table and inserts seed verbatim, then calls cafe, STRASSE, afe, xyz, empty, a in that order. Expected IDs: [1,3], [2], [1,3], [], [], [1,2,3]; compare exact original titles too. Close connection afterward. Read-only queries permit each following action from the unchanged prior state. Local disposable authority permits setup; no account/UI exists. NOT-REPLAYED against product: public function/initializer not authored. Actual consumer output remains due after implementation. Scratch results do not close this case.

Remote permissions, async recovery, external reconciliation and deployed consumer checks have no target in this local requirement. No external access is claimed; any future external consumer boundary remains unverified until authorized and observed.

## Decisions

AD-1: Preserve standard-library stack and existing connection baseline.
AD-2: Select normalized Python linear substring scan of ordered rows from the application connection. Bounded catalog makes the simple scan suitable; handles casefold expansion/interior matches without tokenization. RB-1 supports feasibility. Cost linear in total title length per query; no latency SLA inferred.
AD-3: FTS5/trigram and LIKE are proposals, not requirements. Raw LIKE fails observed required cases; FTS5 is unnecessary and untested.
AD-4: Adopt the minimal table/public API contract above as a planning default; fixture/consumer initialization and durable tests remain future work. No external publication/command is required.

AD-5: Accepted placement default: src.search public search_catalog, private _search_key, existing src.database.connect binding, unittest module and private fixture helpers. Narrow names avoid stdlib shadowing and no existing search symbol collides in inspected inventory. Revalidate imports and discovery after authoring.
AD-6: Accepted ephemeral schema/data policy in Structure; no duplicate-title uniqueness, normalized persisted column or FTS table. JSON originals remain authoritative. Fixture setup is an extension of existing unittest, not a new service/test platform.
AD-7: Accepted synchronous local interaction: Python consumer -> supplied connection SELECT -> temporary normalized comparison -> original result tuples. Caller owns creation, seeding, close and retries after visible exceptions. No async acknowledgment, background work, push channel, long-lived cache or remote deployment. On failure search writes nothing; rerun against initialized connection, do not report false no-results.

## Superseded

Undecided search placement resolved by AD-2/AD-4. Synthetic earlier-stage completion supplies no feature evidence.

# Environment

## Targets and runtimes

Local Python 3.9.6, SQLite 3.54.0, Unicode database 13.0.0, standard library only. Run from repository root. No external endpoint, credentials, network service or deployment is supplied or needed.

## Commands

Full suite, all discovered tests, expected seconds. Currently only test_application_connection exists and passes. Search cases below are PLANNED, not passed.

python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```
Focused search suite, PLANNED after test-spec authors tests/test_search.py; includes all test_search_* cases below; disposable connections, expected seconds. Current replay exits 1: missing module, not feature evidence.

```

## Skills

Delivery: selected ShipLoop and bound Improve, inline. Runner: existing stdlib unittest.

## Harnesses and suites

Definition locator: tests/test_baseline.py. unittest is available: current unchanged baseline ran one passing case (SELECT 1 through database.connect). Historical discovery is synthetic; no feature coverage is implied. No setup repair is required. Reuse TestCase/assertEqual and add tests/test_search.py, class SearchTests. # Offline search delivery plan

## Design basis

Baseline is a connection-only standard-library library with a three-row JSON seed; delta is the search API, not a screen or external deployment. Source baseline evidence: current-system-baseline.md and ../scratch/baseline-and-commands.json. Decisions AD-1..7 in WORKTREE/docs/shiploop/architecture.md and requirements R-1/R-2 in spec.md govern W1. No background acceptance/durable mutation exists, so crash-after-acknowledgment and distributed recovery do not apply; visible sqlite errors and unchanged rows are the applicable recovery checks. Consumer owns connection lifecycle. No UI premise or design tool is applicable to the requested headless API.

## Queue and dependency audit

One coherent W1 deliverable, no independent branches or competing writers. Existing runner/setup is already evidenced; no bootstrap/environment item is needed. The missing reusable facility is a small private fixture extending the existing unittest harness and shares all prerequisites and lifecycle with its only consumer; it belongs first in W1 test-spec, not a new framework or separate stage-only item. No remote delivery/environment requirement exists. Prepare has no new environment provision to perform. This trial stops before prepare.

CLAIM: W1 provides the API, retained regressions and observable consumer results. NEEDS: supplied binding, known schema/seed, normalization contract, runnable suite, independent expected IDs and original strings. SUPPLY: src/database.py and data/catalog.json plus baseline supply existing facts; W1 test-spec supplies disposable fixture/RED cases, W1 implement supplies public API, W1 test supplies regression and consumer outputs. PULL: consumer needs an initialized connection and importable callable, not just a normalization helper; README must show setup before calls. RESOLVE: setup comes before RED assertions and implementation; missing module is expected RED, never a skipped pass. No source edit is needed to collect tests: use method-local import; a missing implementation remains an explicit failing test.

Forward walk: existing connection/JSON -> fixture creates/seeds table -> new tests execute RED on missing function (collection itself succeeds) -> public search function implements read/normalize/filter -> focused/smoke/full suite and public consumer assert literal outputs -> README retains usable setup and results. Each arrow supplies a concrete artifact or observed state, not merely a matching label. Preserve database.connect baseline and JSON strings/IDs.
